text:
maria: Quick sync on benchmark calibration — we need a short SOP for comparing synthetic vs replay runs that actually isolates kernel selection + KV-cache effects.

anand: +1. current runs mix cold-starts, cache warmup, and different kernel choices — results are noisy.

priya: Can we start by defining the primary metrics we care about? I still see people using QPS and goodput interchangeably.

james: My proposal: record TTFT (time-to-first-token), TPOT (time-per-output-token) distribution, p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, and a separate goodput (#user-visible tokens/sec) metric that excludes internal retries and duplicate tokens.

maria: Agree. Also capture model-invocation QPS as a raw request rate. We should report both QPS and goodput side-by-side.

anand: Important: KV cache hit rate and cache warming policy must be part of the run metadata. A 10% hit-rate difference can flip p95 TPOT by a lot for long-context prompts.

priya: For synthetic traffic we must match the sequence-length and prefix-distribution from the replay trace. Otherwise kernel selector picks different kernels and batching behavior diverges.

james: SOP idea: 1) extract trace; 2) compute histograms (seq len, prefix repeats, concurrency); 3) synth generator samples from those histograms; 4) run both synth and replay under same machine config; 5) log kernel traces and KV-cache events.

maria: Also add warmup rules: run 5 minutes warmup or until KV hit-rate stabilizes (delta < 2% over 1m). Log when warmup completed. No measurements during warmup.

anand: For kernel selection diagnostics, dump kernel_id per-layer per-step for a sample subset of requests (e.g., 1/1000) so we can compare kernel paths chosen between synth/replay. Store as lightweight CSV.

perf-bot: [automated] Reminder: include CPU/GPU utilization, kernel ladders, and memory alloc trends. I will attach a perf snapshot when runs complete. :robot_face:

priya: Regression gating: if p95 TPOT regresses > 8% or TTFT p99 regresses > 10% vs baseline, block rollout and open perf issue with traces attached. Baseline must be last-green commit on benchmarking branch.

james: One more: measure cold-start TTFT separately (first request on fresh model worker) vs steady-state TTFT (after warmup). Cold-starts often dominate tail in deduped logs.

maria: Action items: anand - draft the SOP doc with exact commands + log fields; priya - add gating thresholds to CI; james - add kernel_id and KV hit-rate exporters; I'll coordinate a calibration run tomorrow.

anand: Will do. I'll add example grep/awk snippets to extract kernel_id and KV events and a small python parser to compute goodput.

perf-bot: [automated] Saved template: /bench/templates/calibration-v1 — use for initial run.

maria: Great — if anyone sees missing pieces call them out here. Otherwise I'll post a PR with the SOP later today. :thumbsup:
